nodes.summary: Let $f : Q \to Q'$ be a map of states; relabelling by $f$ replaces a state $q$ by $f(q)$ and keeps the halting state. For every action $a$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes and states $Q$ and every configuration $c$ of such a machine, applying $a$ with its successor state relabelled by $f$ to $c$ with its state relabelled by $f$ gives the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$ and then relabelling its state…
nodes.title: Applying a relabelled action

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Let $e_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $e_{\mathrm{out}}$ be injective encodings of types $\alpha$ and $\beta$ as words over the alphabet, $g : \alpha \to \beta$ a function and $t, s : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ bounds. Then $M'$ computes $g$ with respect to these encodings in time $t$…
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves computing a function within time and space bounds

nodes.summary: A deterministic multi-tape Turing machine computes the output $o$ on input $w$ if and only if there is a step $t$ at which the run from the initial configuration on $w$ halts (it is halted after $t$ steps and not halted after any $s < t$ steps) and the configuration it reaches after $t$ steps has output tape $o$.
nodes.title: Computing an output means halting with it

nodes.summary: If a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine runs in time $t$ on input $w$, then for every word $o$ the machine computes $o$ on $w$ if and only if the configuration reached from the initial configuration on $w$ after $t$ steps has output tape $o$.
nodes.title: Output at a time bound

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for all words $x$ and $o$ over the alphabet, $M'$ started on input $x$ eventually halts with output $o$ if and only if $M$ does.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves what a machine computes

nodes.summary: A deterministic machine computes at most one output on an input.
nodes.title: Output determinism

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the alphabet $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every set $L$ of binary words, $M'$ decides $L$ if and only if $M$ decides $L$.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves deciding a language

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a map of states. For every configuration $c$, the configuration obtained from $c$ by replacing its state $q$ by $f(q)$, and keeping the halting state, is halted if and only if $c$ is halted.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves halting

nodes.summary: For a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and steps $s \le t$, if the run from $c$ is halted after $s$ steps, then it is halted after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Halting persists along a run

nodes.summary: If a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine runs in time $t$ on input $w$, then the run from the initial configuration on $w$ is halted after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: A time bound forces halting

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a configuration of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$. If the run from $c$ is not halted after any $s < m$ steps, and the run from the configuration reached after $m$ steps halts at step $n$ (it is halted after $n$ steps and not halted after fewer), then the run from $c$ halts at step $m + n$.
nodes.title: Run composition for halting

nodes.summary: A deterministic multi-tape Turing machine started in a configuration $c$ halts at step $0$ if and only if $c$ is halted.
nodes.title: Halting at step zero

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input word $x$, the initial configuration of $M'$ on $x$ is the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$ with its state $q$ replaced by $f(q)$.
nodes.title: Initial configurations under relabelling

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet, with state sets $Q$ and $Q'$, and let $f : Q \to Q'$. Then $M'$ simulates $M$ up to the relabelling $f$ when the initial state of $M'$ is $f(q_0)$, where $q_0$ is the initial state of $M$, and for every state $q \in Q$, every possibly blank symbol $a$ under the input head and every tuple $w$ of possibly blank symbols under the…
nodes.title: Simulation up to a state relabelling

nodes.summary: Every deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes simulates itself up to the identity relabelling of its states.
nodes.title: Every machine is a relabelling of itself

nodes.summary: For a map $f : Q \to Q'$ of states and an action $a$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes and states $Q$, the relabelled action is the action with states $Q'$ that moves the input head, writes and moves on the work tapes and outputs exactly as $a$ does, and whose successor state is $f(q)$ when $a$ goes to state $q$ and is halting when $a$ halts.
nodes.title: Relabelling the successor state of an action

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet, with state sets $Q$ and $Q'$, such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $f : Q \to Q'$. For a configuration $c$ of $M$, write $f_*(c)$ for the configuration of $M'$ obtained by replacing the state $q$ of $c$ by $f(q)$ and keeping the input head, the work tapes, the work heads and the output (a…
nodes.title: Lockstep runs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input word $x$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration of $M'$ after $t$ steps on input $x$ is the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps on input $x$ with its state relabelled by $f$: a state $q$ becomes $f(q)$ and the halting state stays halting.
nodes.title: Lockstep runs from the initial configuration

nodes.summary: If a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine is halted, then for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ the run from $c$ is in configuration $c$ after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Halted configurations are fixed

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be a transition function that assigns an action to every state, symbol or blank read on the input tape, and tuple of symbols or blanks read on the work tapes, and let $M$ be the deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with initial state $q_0$ and transition function $\delta$. Let $S_\delta$ be the map on configurations that fixes every halted configuration and sends a running configuration in state $q$…
nodes.title: Runs of a machine given by a transition function

nodes.summary: For a configuration $c$ of a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the run from $c$ after $t + 1$ steps is in the same configuration as the run from the successor of $c$ after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Peeling off the first step of a run

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $c$ a configuration of $M$ and $m, n$ natural numbers. If $M$ started in $c$ halts at step $m + n$, that is, it is halted after $m + n$ steps and not halted after any fewer, then $M$ started in the configuration reached from $c$ after $m$ steps halts at step $n$.
nodes.title: Halting step after a run prefix

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $M$ runs in space $s$ on $x$, that is, every computation path of $M$ on $x$ visits at most $s$ work-tape cells, if and only if for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ the run of $M$ from the initial configuration on $x$ visits at most $s$ work-tape cells within its first $t$ steps. Visited cells are counted on each work tape…
nodes.title: Space bounds of deterministic machines

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input $x$ and every $s \in \mathbb{N}$, $M'$ runs in space $s$ on $x$ if and only if $M$ runs in space $s$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves space bounds

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $w$ an input and $t$ a natural number. Then $M$ runs in time $t$ on $w$, that is, every computation path of $M$ on $w$ with at least $t$ steps ends in a halted configuration, if and only if $M$ started in its initial configuration on $w$ is halted after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Time bounds of deterministic machines

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to a state relabelling $f$. Then for every input $x$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $M'$ runs in time $t$ on $x$ if and only if $M$ runs in time $t$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves time bounds

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $x$ an input and $t \in \mathbb{N}$. The number of work-tape cells visited along the computation path of $M$ on $x$ made of the first $t$ steps from the initial configuration equals the space used by the run of $M$ from the initial configuration on $x$ up to step $t$. Both count the visited cells on each work tape separately and sum over the work tapes.
nodes.title: Space of the deterministic computation path

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, with the one-step relation it inherits as a nondeterministic machine. If a configuration $c$ steps to both $c_1$ and $c_2$, then $c_1 = c_2$.
nodes.title: Step determinism

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be the deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with initial state $q_0$ and transition function $\delta$. For every configuration $c$, the step of $M$ from $c$ is the successor of $c$ under $\delta$: $c$ itself if $c$ is halted, and otherwise the result of applying to $c$ the action that $\delta$ selects for the state of $c$ and the symbols under its input and work tape heads.
nodes.title: Step of a machine given by a transition function

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be a transition function of a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, assigning an action to each state, input symbol and tuple of $k$ work tape symbols, where a symbol may be blank. The successor of a configuration $c$ under $\delta$ is $c$ itself if $c$ is halted, and otherwise the configuration obtained by applying to $c$ the action $\delta(q, a, b)$, where $q$ is the state of $c$, $a$ the…
nodes.title: Successor under a transition function

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet, with state sets $Q$ and $Q'$, such that $M'$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $f : Q \to Q'$. For a configuration $c$ of $M$, write $f_*(c)$ for the configuration of $M'$ obtained by replacing the state $q$ of $c$ by $f(q)$ and keeping the input head, the work tapes, the work heads and the output (a…
nodes.title: Relabelled machines step in lockstep

nodes.summary: Let $M$, $M'$ and $M''$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and the same alphabet, with state sets $Q$, $Q'$ and $Q''$. If $M'$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $f : Q \to Q'$ and $M''$ simulates $M'$ up to the state relabelling $g : Q' \to Q''$, then $M''$ simulates $M$ up to the state relabelling $g \circ f$.
nodes.title: Relabellings compose

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
